# Japan Trip Planning

I have been looking forward to this for months. Finally pulling together all the details for the upcoming Japan adventure. The trip is shaping up nicely although there are still a few loose ends to tie up before I feel fully prepared. Spring should be a beautiful time to visit with the tail end of cherry blossoms possibly still around in some places.

## Flight Details
Flights are officially booked. Flying out of [[JFK]] to [[Haneda Airport]] on ANA departing May 28 and returning June 11. The confirmation code is **K7QW2P**. I went ahead and added the flight details to my calendar and set reminders for check in. The outbound flight leaves in the evening so I should be able to get a decent amount of sleep on the plane. Return flight arrives back at JFK in the early afternoon which will help with jet lag adjustment on the way home.

I still need to decide on the exact arrival and departure times so I can plan the first and last days better. The layover on the way there is pretty short so I hope there are no delays.

## Transportation
After doing quite a bit of research I have decided that a [[JR Pass]] is not worth it for this itinerary. The places I am visiting are mostly concentrated in the Kyoto and Tokyo areas and the pass would not save enough to justify the cost. Will just buy individual tickets as needed. The [[Suica card]] or [[ICOCA card]] will probably be my best friend for local trains and buses. Need to remember to pick one up at the airport.

## Accommodation
The [[Airbnb in Kyoto]] is confirmed for May 31 through June 4. It looks like a traditional style place with tatami mats and a small balcony overlooking a quiet street. The host seems very responsive which is reassuring. Still need to book the Tokyo portion of the stay. Probably looking at something central like Shinjuku or Shibuya for the first few nights and then maybe near Asakusa for the last part of the trip. Have a few listings saved to compare.

## Itinerary
Still very much a work in progress. The rough outline looks like this:

- May 28: Depart JFK
- May 29: Arrive Haneda, travel to Tokyo, light first day exploring
- May 31: Travel to Kyoto, check into Airbnb
- June 1-3: Full days in Kyoto (temples, food tour, Arashiyama)
- June 4: Return to Tokyo
- June 5-9: Tokyo sights (museums, markets, day trip possibilities)
- June 11: Return flight

I want to leave some flexibility for spontaneous activities. Maybe add a day trip to [[Nara]] or [[Hakone]] if energy levels allow. Still debating whether to include Hiroshima or keep things more relaxed.

## Packing List
Starting to think about what to bring. Japan in late spring can be warm during the day but cooler in the evenings. Definitely need comfortable walking shoes because there will be a lot of miles on my feet. Planning to pack light with a carry-on only approach if possible. Current list includes:

- Lightweight rain jacket (just in case)
- Comfortable sneakers and sandals
- Power adapter and portable charger
- Small daypack
- Reusable water bottle
- Some basic medications and prescriptions
- Modest clothing for temple visits

Still need to refine this. The [[packing-list]] note has some good ideas I can pull from.

## Budget
Total trip budget set at $3,200 including flights, accommodation, food, transportation and activities. Flights took a good chunk already so I need to be mindful of daily spending. Breaking it down roughly:

- Flights: ~$1,150
- Accommodation: ~$650
- Food: $600 (trying to keep it reasonable but also experience the food scene)
- Local transport: $250
- Activities and misc: $550

This leaves a little buffer which is smart. I will track expenses daily in a separate note to make sure things stay on track. Eating at convenience stores and local places will help keep costs down while still enjoying great food.

## Open Questions
- Should I book the Tokyo hotels now or wait for better deals closer to the date?
- Is it worth getting a pocket wifi or just rely on data on my phone?
- Any specific festivals or events happening during these dates?
- How many day trips make sense without burning out?
- Vegetarian restaurant recommendations for Kyoto?

I need to do some more research on these points this weekend. Maybe reach out to [[Sarah]] who went last year for her recommendations. Also should check current entry requirements and make sure my passport is up to date.

Feeling excited but also a bit overwhelmed with all the planning. Taking it one section at a time seems to be working. Will update this note as decisions get made and new ideas come up. Cannot wait to walk through Kyoto streets and try all the street food.
